findings.issue_text: `isAccessTokenId` extracts the wrong substring (`substring(3, 5)`) and rejects it when it equals the expected shortcut, so assertions accept tokens with any expected grant shortcut instead of validating grant encoding.
Adding abstract `getShortcut()` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` breaks existing external implementations: compiled providers can throw `AbstractMethodError` and source implementations no longer compile.
Grant shortcuts are not enforced as exactly two characters, so custom providers returning 1- or 3-character shortcuts can mint token IDs rejected by `getTokenContextFromTokenId`.
`AccessTokenContext` validates `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`, allowing a null raw ID to be encoded as the literal `"null"`.

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding abstract `getShortcut()` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` breaks existing external implementations: compiled providers can throw `AbstractMethodError` and source implementations no longer compile.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line: `String getShortcut();`). This is a breaking change for any existing external implementations of this interface. When existing compiled providers that implement `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` are loaded, they will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime because they don't implement the new method. Source implementations will fail to compile. This is a real backward compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant shortcuts are not enforced as exactly two characters, so custom providers returning 1- or 3-character shortcuts can mint token IDs rejected by `getTokenContextFromTokenId`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java` expects exactly 6 characters for the encoded context (line 79: `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)`), with the grant type shortcut being characters 4-6 (2 chars). The `encodeTokenId` method concatenates shortcuts directly. However, the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` interface added in the diff has no validation enforcing exactly 2 characters. While all built-in implementations use 2-char shortcuts (ac, cc, pg, pc, rt, ro, te, ci, dg), custom providers could return shortcuts of different lengths, causing token IDs that would fail parsing with 'Expected length of 6' error. This is a real validation gap between encoding and the interface contract.
